title: Guiding Principles of Good AI Practice in Drug Development
journal_or_venue: U.S. Food and Drug Administration and European Medicines Agency

content.abstract_summary: FDA and EMA jointly set out ten principles for AI use in drug development, including a risk-based approach, clear context of use, data governance, lifecycle management, risk-based performance assessment, and clear essential information.
key_findings: The principles address AI evidence generation across the medicine lifecycle.
They explicitly emphasize data governance, documentation, risk-based assessment, and lifecycle management.
They are intended to inform future good practice and international convergence, not to prescribe a single technical method.
limitations: Principles are high-level and do not specify pharmacometric implementation details or quantitative acceptance criteria.

gaps_addressed: AI lifecycle, data governance, risk-based performance assessment, and essential reporting in drug development

provenance.notes: Primary joint FDA-EMA principles published January 2026.
